clue.text: Composer at the piano maybe making fresh arrangement of A, B, C etc.

definitions.text: fresh arrangement of A, B, C etc.

parts.note: Antonin Dvorak was the Czech composer of the New World Symphony
a piano is one example of an instrument with a keyboard

explanation.surface: A composer seated at the piano working up a new arrangement of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement' and 'composer' together suggest music, but the A, B, C are the letters on a typing layout, not musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dvorak layout is an alternative typewriter key layout that reorders the letters of the standard QWERTY design.

clue.text: Long-winded poem swallows half of book

indicators.note: swallows means the poem takes the following letters inside it

parts.note: a verse is a poem

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word is its first two letters

explanation.surface: A tedious poem that devours half a book's length.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbose writing uses more words than needed, which is wordy or rambling.

clue.text: Rebels imprisoning family with son showing dangerous attitude

indicators.note: imprisoning says the rebel word holds the family word inside

parts.note: rebels as a verb, someone who rises up rises against authority
kin is family

explanation.surface: Insurgents taking a family hostage, with a son showing a reckless streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rebels' looks like a noun but is the verb RISES, which holds KIN, then S.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskiness is a hazardous quality, a readiness to court danger.

clue.text: Look for getting high, inhaling new joints …

indicators.note: inhaling means the reversed word takes the next letter inside it
getting high in a down clue means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: to seek is to look for

explanation.surface: Someone looking to get high, breathing in from fresh joints of cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting high' reverses SEEK to KEES, and 'inhaling' puts N inside. 'joints' looks like cannabis but means body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the joint between the thigh and the lower leg.

clue.text: … ecstatic, ingesting tab, getting very high

indicators.note: ingesting says the ecstatic word swallows the following letters

parts.note: elated means ecstatic
E is a tablet of ecstasy in drug slang

explanation.surface: Continuing the drug story: someone euphoric after swallowing a pill and getting very stoned.
explanation.walkthrough: E and V go inside ELATED. 'high' looks like drug slang to match the surface but means raised up.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevated means raised to a height, so lofty or high up.

clue.text: Amount of data from most of sample

parts.note: by can mean from, as in a work by an author

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the sample word is dropped

parts.note: a test is a sample, as in a blood test

explanation.surface: A statistician working out how much data can be drawn from most of a sample.
explanation.definitionFit: Data size is measured in units of eight bits, so these units together are an amount of data.

clue.text: Mean to claim head off court servant

parts.note: to aver is to claim or assert

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the servant word is removed

parts.note: a page is a boy servant at a royal court

explanation.surface: Someone means to accuse a royal servant of losing his head.
explanation.definitionFit: The mean and the average are both statistical names for a central value.

clue.text: Guard retaining energy after extremes of deadly disease

indicators.note: after places the guard piece behind the extremes of deadly
the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, from deadly
retaining means the guard word holds the energy letter inside

parts.note: a sentry is a guard
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sentry keeping up his strength despite a deadly sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Dysentery is an infection of the intestines causing severe diarrhoea, an illness.

clue.text: Bill turned up around old ship

indicators.note: around says the reversed bill encloses the next letter
turned up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as at a bar

explanation.surface: A bill appearing for an old ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Boat is used loosely for any vessel, including a ship.

clue.text: A rootstock is linked to indicator of alternative source of roughage

parts.note: the word or signals an alternative, as in tea or coffee

indicators.note: the source of a word is its beginning, so take the opening letter of roughage

explanation.surface: A gardener's or dietitian's note about a plant root used as a fibre source.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris root is the fragrant underground stem of certain irises, used in perfumery, so it is a kind of rootstock.

clue.text: English candour avoided by detective showing upright nature

indicators.note: the detective's letters are kept out of the word for candour, removed from it

parts.note: candour, plain speaking, is directness
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: An English witness whose frankness a detective sidesteps, though they seem upstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoided by' means the Detective Inspector's letters are taken out of the word for candour.
explanation.definitionFit: Being erect means standing straight, so the quality is an upright posture or nature.

clue.text: Science taken aback after harbour overturned in equatorial region

indicators.note: after places the science piece behind the harbour piece
overturned says the word for harbour is turned round

parts.note: a port is a harbour

indicators.note: taken aback, read literally, puts the short word for science back to front

explanation.surface: A scientist startled on finding a harbour capsized somewhere near the equator.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'overturned' and 'taken aback' signal reversals; 'after' puts the science piece second, though it comes first in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics are the band of the earth either side of the equator, between Cancer and Capricorn.

clue.text: Decline to participate in getting behind travel agents around start of summer

indicators.note: getting behind puts the word in after the rest
around says the letters of the travel body enclose the next piece

parts.note: ABTA is the Association of British Travel Agents

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, taken from summer

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Refusing to join a group of travel agents promoting the summer season.
explanation.walkthrough: ABTA is the British travel agents' trade association, familiar from holiday brochures; 'getting behind' puts the final piece at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to refrain from taking part, especially from voting.

clue.text: Caught, chopped and chomped

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
to hew is to chop, as with an axe

explanation.surface: A list of things done to a piece of food on its way to being eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To chomp is to munch noisily, which is a vigorous way of chewing food.

clue.text: Pitiless truth represented in film

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters sit inside the film word

parts.note: a coat is a thin film or layer, as of paint

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A harsh truth depicted in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a movie but means a thin layer; 'represented' signals the rearrangement that sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutthroat means ruthless or merciless, as in cutthroat competition.

clue.text: What lawyer writes, accounting for storms in sheltered area

indicators.note: accounting for means taking in, so the sheltered area contains the storms

parts.note: the lee is the side sheltered from the wind
gales are storms

explanation.surface: A lawyer drafting an insurance claim for storm damage in a sheltered spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalese is the dense jargon used in legal documents, the style lawyers draft in.

clue.text: High honour in coming in to reduce hate

indicators.note: coming in to says the honour and in go inside the word for reduce

parts.note: to abate is to reduce or lessen
OM is the Order of Merit, a high British honour
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grand honour arriving in time to lessen someone's hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: The Order of Merit (OM) is a British honour limited to a few members.
explanation.definitionFit: To abominate is to loathe or detest, a strong synonym for hate.

clue.text: Insect boy picked up beside one road

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the word is lifted, read upwards

parts.note: by means beside, as in by the sea
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boy lifting a beetle by the roadside.
explanation.definitionFit: The ladybird is a small, spotted red beetle, a common insect.

clue.text: Charm? Some sentimentalism anyway

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a lucky charm is just a bit of sentiment after all.
explanation.definitionFit: A lucky charm is an object believed to bring good fortune or ward off harm, like an amulet.

clue.text: Desk and other things turning up in possession of the French navy

indicators.note: in possession of means held by, so the reversed piece sits inside the French and navy letters

parts.note: le is French for the
RN is the Royal Navy

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: etc is short for et cetera, meaning and other things

explanation.surface: A desk and miscellany found among the French navy's property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses the short form for other things, and 'in possession of' puts it inside the French article plus the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a reading stand with a sloping top, a kind of desk for a speaker.

clue.text: Academic taking on significant example of idiocy

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
key means important or significant

explanation.surface: A scholar taking on a notable case study in foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is a slang term for a fool, so it stands for a person showing stupidity.

clue.text: Bird of prey picked up vegetable, strong in grip

indicators.note: in grip means held tight inside the reversed vegetable
picked up in a down clue means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a leek is a vegetable

explanation.surface: A hawk swooping to seize a vegetable and holding it firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' reverses the vegetable to give KEEL, and 'in grip' has that hold the abbreviation for strong.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon that hovers before swooping, a raptor.

clue.text: Journalist longing to go over part of London

parts.note: hack is slang for a journalist

indicators.note: to go over here means to turn over, reading the word for longing backwards

parts.note: a yen is a longing

explanation.surface: A reporter yearning to cross into a particular district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go over' reverses the Japanese-currency word for longing; Hackney is an inner London borough.
explanation.definitionFit: Hackney is a borough in the east of London.

clue.text: Low point provides new attitude about depth

indicators.note: about says the attitude word goes round the depth letter

parts.note: an air is a manner or attitude

explanation.surface: A low moment brings a fresh outlook on how deep things go.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, the opposite of the zenith.

clue.text: Causes excitement in prison with drink

parts.note: stir is slang for prison
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A jail where drink is smuggled in, causing a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble or a crowd is to provoke agitation or arouse feeling.

clue.text: Angry outburst observed on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than read, so the word sounds the same

parts.note: something observed has been seen

explanation.surface: A furious tirade that listeners noticed during a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a scene means causing a public display of temper or emotion.

clue.text: Church features mostly cleaned up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the shortened word is read upwards
mostly means all but the last letter of the cleaned word

parts.note: swept means cleaned with a broom

explanation.surface: Parts of a church that have been mostly tidied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts SWEPT to SWEP and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pews are the long wooden benches for the congregation, fixtures in a church.

clue.text: No longer bothered by Verdi works showing greater activity

parts.note: something over is finished, no longer happening

indicators.note: works is read as a verb, the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone no longer troubled by Verdi's operas, now showing more energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges VERDI into DRIVE; 'works' looks like a noun for Verdi's operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Going into overdrive means operating at a heightened, frenetic level of effort.

clue.text: Cart ignoring first symbol on road sign

indicators.note: ignoring first means the opening letter of the cart word is dropped

parts.note: a barrow is a small cart

explanation.surface: A cart driver paying no attention to the first road sign.
explanation.definitionFit: Directions on traffic signs are typically shown by a pointed line, the head of a bow's missile.

clue.text: Passage connecting successfully into barrels in Kent town

indicators.note: into says the passage and the adverb are put inside the barrels

parts.note: tuns are large casks or barrels
a bridge is a passage connecting two sides
well means successfully

explanation.surface: Smugglers successfully run a tunnel into a stack of barrels in a Kent town.
explanation.definitionFit: Royal Tunbridge Wells is a spa town in the English county of Kent, famous for its stuffy letter-writers.
